criteria.description: Public review submission reports start, continuing human progress, one final outcome, and one final JSON document in structured mode.
criteria.evidence: traceability.md US1.1; integrated exact-entry human progress and singular JSON tests
criteria.notes: Verify exact public-entry human and structured-output behavior.

criteria.description: Review admission is atomic: transition occurs only after admission; timeout, cancellation, and blocking preserve the prior lane.
criteria.evidence: traceability.md US1.2/US1.3; integrated success, timeout, cancellation, and mutation assertions
criteria.notes: Verify mutation ordering and zero-transition terminal outcomes.

criteria.description: Explicit per-invocation skip bypasses gate execution and reports the skip reason in human and structured output.
criteria.evidence: traceability.md US2.1; integrated exact-entry skip precedence tests
criteria.notes: Verify no validation subprocess or wait occurs.

criteria.description: Truthy disable controls suppress gate execution and implicit daemon startup without suppressing explicit daemon management.
criteria.evidence: traceability.md US2.2; integrated disable controls and daemon-exception tests
criteria.notes: Verify both canonical disable controls and daemon exception.

criteria.description: Canonical new failures warn and admit by default, while explicit project policy can block the same verdict.
criteria.evidence: integrated test_pre_review_gate_integration warn/block/force scenarios through the real ACTIVE binding
criteria.notes: Verify real public auto-derived warn, block, and force paths.

criteria.description: Timeout and catchable cancellation reap the owned validation tree without transition; abrupt parent death preserves lane/event integrity.
criteria.evidence: traceability.md interruption rows; integrated process-tree and parent-death tests
criteria.notes: Uncatchable hard-kill orphan cleanup remains explicitly out of scope.

criteria.description: Skip, disable controls, gate execution, policy, and deadline races follow the specified deterministic precedence.
criteria.evidence: traceability.md precedence and deadline-race rows; integrated public and process-tree suites
criteria.notes: Verify precedence combinations and both deadline race outcomes.

criteria.description: The ordinary successful review-submission flow remains compatible when no exceptional control or verdict applies.
criteria.evidence: traceability.md US1.2/US2.3; integrated registered-binding and existing-transition scenarios
criteria.notes: Verify normal registered binding and existing transition behavior.

criteria.description: Deterministically oversized scope is refused before candidate launch, without transition or automatic skip, and reports both recovery choices.
criteria.evidence: traceability.md US1.4; integrated exact-entry oversized refusal and gate-budget tests
criteria.notes: Verify exact and superset oversized scopes plus unknown descendant behavior.

criteria.description: Unknown-budget timeout reports normalized identity, targets, configured budget, monotonic elapsed time, unchanged lane, and metadata-candidate guidance.
criteria.evidence: traceability.md unknown-timeout row; integrated real-evaluator exact-entry human and JSON evidence
criteria.notes: Verify diagnostic evidence without runtime policy mutation.

negative_invariants.description: No asynchronous review job or pending-review lane/state is introduced.
New regressions remain warn-by-default unless blocking is explicitly configured.
No alternate pending_review lifecycle vocabulary or status authority is introduced.
Existing pre-review behavior is preserved while only demonstrated gaps are changed.
Skip and disable recovery paths use supported lifecycle controls without direct event or lane mutation.
Structured mode emits one final JSON document without NDJSON or mixed progress output.
Runtime observations never mutate or promote deterministic budget metadata automatically.
